name: Ballot Referenda
description: Questions the council considered putting to Chicago voters, including gunshot detection technology.
summary: The City Council considered several referenda questions for Chicago voters. The most prominent was R2026-0025451, a proposed November 3, 2026 general election question on whether Chicago should restart use of gunshot detection technology that informs first responders when gunshots are detected; introduced 2026-05-20, it was considered by the Committee on Committees and Rules on 2026-07-09, adopted by voice vote in committee [11], and adopted by the City Council 49 Yea / 0 Nay on 2026-07-15. A companion citywide question, R2026-0025459, on a permanent festival and outdoor event measure, followed the same path and was also adopted 49 Yea / 0 Nay on 2026-07-15. By contrast, R2025-0018197, a March 17, 2026 primary election question on establishing a 100-day non-salaried Office, introduced 2025-06-18 and still in committee, was Recommended for Re-Referral by the City Council 15 Yea / 30 Nay on 2026-05-20, leaving its fate unresolved. A related ranked-choice voting referendum (R2025-0018786) was re-referred to the Committee on Committees and Rules per the 2026-07-09 meeting summary [9], and a 26th Ward shared-housing referendum (SR2025-0021045) was adopted as substituted. Committee hearings on 2026-07-07 covered election administration topics including vote-by-mail return options, universal vote centers, and ballot-on-demand modernization [2][4][5][8], but the record trail does not show final disposition of the re-referred referenda, which remain open.
one_line: Gunshot detection and festival referenda adopted 49-0 on 2026-07-15; 100-day office question re-referred 15-30, unresolved.
